root_cause: Table._get_padding_width (used by _measure_column to size columns) ignored pad_edge, while the render-time get_padding in Table._get_cells zeroes the left padding of the first column and the right padding of the last column when pad_edge=False. Table.grid defaults pad_edge=False, collapse_padding=True, so with padding=(0,1) the first column was measured 1 cell wider (left pad counted but never rendered) and the last column 1 cell wider (right pad counted but never rendered). Result: 'aaa  aaa aaa ' (double gap after col 0, trailing space) instead of 'aaa aaa aaa'.
best_solution: Make measurement agree with rendering. In rich/table.py Table._get_padding_width(column_index), after the collapse_padding adjustment add: if not self.pad_edge: if column_index == 0: pad_left = 0; if column_index == len(self.columns) - 1: pad_right = 0. Gold also rewrote the collapse branch to pad_left = 0; pad_right = abs(pad_left - pad_right) (i.e. collapse drops the left pad on every column), which is identical to the old max(0, left-right) behavior for symmetric padding. The other 4 hunks are blank-line whitespace only. Reasoning path from the title: grep 'padding_width' -> Table._get_padding_width; compare with get_padding() in _get_cells, which handles pad_edge; the measuring copy does not, so widths drift by the edge padding.
acceptable_alternatives: Adding only the pad_edge zeroing to _get_padding_width while keeping the old collapse_padding logic passes both hidden tests (Columns and the grid test use symmetric padding (0,1), where old and new collapse logic coincide). Refactoring so measurement and render share one padding helper would also work.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_table.py::test_padding_width (new): Table.grid(padding=(0,1)) with 3 columns width=3, one row of 'aaa' cells, Console(record=True).export_text(styles=True) must equal exactly 'aaa aaa aaa\n'. tests/test_columns.py::test_render: updated golden output, the 'fixed width' section of Columns (built on Table.grid, pad_edge=False) now has first column one char narrower and no trailing pad on the last column (e.g. 'Anteater,        Eunectes sp. ... Ursus americanus\n').
locating_signals: Statement is only 'fix for padding width' plus the issue URL; the issue text (Table.grid padding double gap after first column) is not shown to the agent. The phrase 'padding width' maps literally to the private method Table._get_padding_width in rich/table.py; grepping 'padding_width' finds it immediately. The word 'padding' alone misleads toward rich/padding.py (Padding class).
our_outcome_summary: All four configs failed in the Kaggle env. v4, v6 and v7 produced the identical wrong-location patch: in rich/padding.py Padding.__rich_console__ they clamped render width with max(0, width - self.left - self.right), a guard against negative widths that has nothing to do with table column measurement; v7 additionally committed a stray repro_padding.py. rich/table.py was never touched, so test_padding_width still produced 'aaa  aaa aaa \n' and test_columns::test_render still had the old fixed-width golden output (2 failed, 20 passed). v8 hit the 300 s budget with an empty patch.
generalizable_lesson: When the statement is a terse title (e.g. 'fix for X Y') with only an issue link, grep the codebase for the title words joined as an identifier (x_y, xY, get_x_y) before grepping the loose noun; a literal method-name match is usually the gold location. For layout/rendering bugs, look for two code paths that compute the same quantity (measure vs render, size estimate vs actual draw) and make the measuring path honor every flag the rendering path honors (edge/first/last special cases). Write a tiny repro that prints repr() of the output and check exact spacing before patching a generic helper.
